name: fbgemm_pack_quantized_matrix
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::fbgemm_pack_quantized_matrix(Tensor input) -> Tensor. This signature is representative only; original Gems pytest owns the complete contract for every overload, positional call form, keyword argument, return, raised error, aliasing and mutation, and must not be narrowed to this one signature. Supplied registered schema strings verbatim: `aten::fbgemm_pack_quantized_matrix(Tensor input) -> Tensor`; `aten::fbgemm_pack_quantized_matrix.KN(Tensor input, int K, int N) -> Tensor`. The non-representative .KN overload adds required int packing dimensions K and N and is exercised both as torch.ops.aten.fbgemm_pack_quantized_matrix(input, K, N) and flag_gems.fbgemm_pack_quantized_matrix(inp, K, N); those extra arguments and their error handling stay in the pytest. Semantics: CPU-only FBGEMM int8 host packer. The input must be dtype int8 with rank >= 2, and the result is a fixed-size one-dimensional uint8 descriptor that wraps library heap state, so two independently allocated handles are never compared byte-wise; the packed payload is validated through the genuine native consumer torch.ops.aten.fbgemm_linear_int8_weight_fp32_activation (and the quantizer torch.ops.aten.fbgemm_linear_quantize_weight), with the descriptor also checked for dtype, rank, shape, stride, numel and device. Non-int8 dtypes, rank < 2, non-tensor inputs and non-integer or missing K/N are rejected by native dtype and schema/parser checks; the NaN/Inf special-value rows use float32/float16/bfloat16 inputs and assert rejection of those float dtypes, since int8 cannot represent NaN/Inf and the native checks dispatch on dtype rather than inspecting payload values.
